📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Cherry has done it once again with its eccentric reveals, as its latest livestream presentation Cherry Time has revealed not only the release date for the upcoming DLC for Hollow Knight: Silksong, but also some brand-newly introduced original titles.

Previously known mostly for the original Hollow Knight, the studio is now expanding its catalogue to actually include some more indie titles from different genres, but not without giving some love to the original game that first made them famous.

Sea of Sorrow, a free expansion adding tons of fresh areas, bosses, challenges, quality-of-life improvements, and some new lore pieces for Silksong, is described as an “expansion like they never did before” and will be dropping on December 11, free for all players.

According to recent reports, the Cherry Time livestream has revealed the latest trailer for the Silksong expansion, complete with its release date and a small tease for its bosses. Just like with the base game, the release date was revealed exactly two weeks before its launch.

According to recent reports, first announced earlier this week, the stream was a welcome surprise for the fans, filled with new footage from the new areas Hornet will visit and small showcases of what we can expect in this new adventure. And if we can take the original Hollow Knight expansions as a baseline, we’re in for a huge treat here.

It has been revealed that we can see upcoming scenes of Hornet running across the new areas and the new enemies she’ll be facing in these distant waters. A favorite of mine is the new pirate-like boss, which is one of the main focuses in this trailer. We can also see some platforming sessions and at least one new of the dreaded enemy gauntlets in the trailer, so get ready to put those tools to use.

Recent findings suggest that and speaking of tools, the biggest highlight obviously goes to the final scene, where Hornet actually unveils a fresh tool being used for the most ancient practice in any good RPG: fishing. Love it or hate it, the game wouldn’t be complete without it, and you know it. And in classic Hollow Knight fashion, expect some obscure secret to be hidden beneath the fishing waters.

For now, I’m hoping for more challenging areas such as the Cogwork Core and fewer areas that are just a torture session in a trench coat, such as Bilewater.

Sources indicate that aside from Sea of Sorrow news, Team Cherry also promised more “exciting announcements”, and they did deliver. Previously known as the studio that wouldn’t speak with its public while working on their game (in a very justified way), this now seems to be in the past as the small South Australian studio came forward not only with a release date for the expansion, but also with brand-new titles developed by the studio.

These include Blokan: Secret of the Walking City, a new game by Hollow Knight artist Rohan Fraser. It follows a detective solving cases in a traditional puzzle game style above a fantasy-inspired city, fully drawn by hand. It is inspired by the traditional golden age adventure games, according to Fraser himself.

Sources indicate that radio Rain is another one, a side-scrolling title made by Lukas Stobie, who previously developed Rising Dusk. This fresh side-scrolling adventure game follows the protagonist as she finds her way across the ruins of a rainy world filled with music, all in an amazing pixel art style.

In a recent development, the final reveal is The Botanist and The Translator, developed by Makoto Kuji (the voice of Hornet herself). In this 2d adventure game, you’ll play as the botanist-investigator Hatti and her animal translator partner Oliver, who work together to unveil a mystery while exploring a beautifully hand-drawn Sailor Moon-inspired world.

It’s amazing to see Team Cherry actually growing up as a studio, as they can now reliably deliver more titles and not be bound to the same franchise for years. While the Hollow Knight games might still be their magnum opus, knowing that we’ll see more of its DNA implemented across different titles is an even better gift than I could’ve asked for. Especially now that Sea of Sorrow is coming.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

In a recent development, this is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

First, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

Next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

For a whole lot more on Grand Theft Auto VI, head here.

Industry observers note that bad signal or dead zones? Download your issues before you leave and read anywhere.

Rule the roads without the stress!

Picture yourself cruising down a wide-open road with nothing but your thoughts and your truck with you - if that's possibly the most relaxing thing you can ever imagine, then Highway Heroes might just be your cup of tea.

Pixel Federation's truck tycoon is more than just getting cargo from one spot to another - nor is it all about the stress of keeping a trucking empire afloat. If you still haven't gotten on board with Highway Heroes, here's why you should!

It's essentially a different way of unwinding after a long and hard day, where you can watch your trucks move through a handcrafted map inspired by America in full 3D. It's not just soulless icons that drive here and there - you can marvel at the fruits of your labour as your trucks travel on the road, offering a more meditative experience all throughout. Less about speed, more about strategy That means it's not like other tycoon truck games where speed is of the essence - here, it's really all about smart planning and making sure you strategise every move to keep your business running.

Industry observers note that whether that's figuring out how to handle a certain request depending on your capacity or upgrading your fleet to expand your operations, your decision-making matters more than simply keeping things ticking over. And with your strategies comes the satisfaction of pulling things off in the end too, which adds to the relaxation at the end of the day. Cool customisations for your entire collection More than just a transport game, Highway Heroes is also a truck game, so to speak, so you can expect to spruce up your entire fleet depending on your tastes. As you progress through the levels, you get to unlock more and more cosmetics to help you customise your fleet. Plus, you'll discover rigs and upgrade them to personalise your trucks to your liking.

That's where the beauty of being able to zoom in and out of those 3D truck models comes into play too, by the way - seeing how every detail you've customised reflects onto your fleet certainly adds to the enjoyment of watching your trucks go by. Real-world looks without the real-world stress With idle mechanics thrown into the mix, the transport manager also keeps the real-world stress at bay without compromising on real-world quality. This means that trucks and environments are incredibly detailed, with new regions popping up continuously and themed events keeping things fresh.

The recent Gold Fever, Rocket Runway, and Haul-O-Ween events, for instance, keep the cargo game fresh and continue to immerse players in American trucking culture - as approved by trucking veterans worldwide.

If you're on the hunt for a relaxing yet strategically satisfying truck tycoon sim that respects your time (and taste!), Highway Heroes' realistic trucks and relaxing gameplay might just do the trick.

Highway Heroes is available to download right now from the App Store and Google Play. It’s a free-to-play game with optional in-app purchases available.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

Recent findings suggest that so, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

The third upper-bracket quarter-final of the VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 needed a deciding third map.

  • Sources indicate that the major fresh arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest massive content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

According to recent reports, this one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

Sources indicate that the major fresh arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

According to recent reports, the reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

It has been revealed that staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Sources indicate that outside of events, there’s a newly introduced set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Catch up on the latest set of Genshin Impact codes before you play, and check out why we think Genshin Impact is one of the best mobile games you can play today.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newly introduced Radical Games has had its unannounced project canceled according to a developer, with the studio speculated to have been working on a The Simpsons: Hit & Run remake.

Earlier this year, Simpsons creator Matt Groening casually dropped the news that something to do with The Simpsons: Hit & Run was happening, saying at a D23 panel that "the original game is coming back in some form." This, mixed with New Radical's now-deleted LinkedIn hiring post that mentioned "our stylized game" which would naturally fit with The Simpsons, had folks speculating that the studio – partially comprised of devs from OG Hit & Run studio, Radical Entertainment – might be working on a remake.

Sources indicate that however, whatever the studio was working on has now unfortunately been scrapped. Darren Evenson – senior game designer at New Radical Games – posts on LinkedIn saying the devs' latest project "was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations.".

According to recent reports, while The Simpsons link is still unconfirmed, Evenson writes "if you don't make the money, then you don't get the power" which is a reference to Scarface – which Radical also worked on a game for. However, this line was famously parodied in The Simpsons when Homer has his giant pile of sugar in the backyard. I could be reading entirely too much into it, but that could be a hint that this was sadly a Hit & Run remaster that was canned.

Sources indicate that needless to say, fans aren't happy. "I'm never going to emotionally recover from this," one indicates on Twitter in response. "Yeah bro is paraphrasing a quote from Homer it's over boys," speculates another.

There's no wonder the news is having such an impact, even without confirmation that a remake was definitely canceled. Sure, GTA 6 is the highest-rated game of all time and people were waiting 13 years for it to come out, but after 23 years, The Simpsons Hit & Run was the real open-world car-stealing game that everyone was waiting to see get a follow-up.

The iconic licensed title is still one of the most beloved games ever made, and fans have been asking for a sequel for decades, but despite its massive success – and reports emerging that there was a sequel in the works – one never came to fruition. The unrelated The Simpsons Game was the only console game the franchise has had since.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The substantial 2026 is almost over, and if you work at Relic Entertainment or are a Firm of Heroes fan like me, it’s fair to say this year has been a strong one for the franchise.

The classic real-time strategy franchise has brought Company of Heroes 3 into maturity with patch 3.0, and has dared to go beyond the battlegroup packs for the first time with not one but two DLCs that finally enhance single-player gameplay to a significant extent.

This Wednesday, just in time for the Thanksgiving break, Relic released the Operation Torch campaign DLC for Tech giant of Heroes 3. The campaign has proven divisive, presently sitting with mixed Steam reviews and sparking either love or disappointment from critics.

One thing everyone seems to agree on, however, is that one mission in particular was a tough sell, and it looks like Relic Entertainment has gotten the hint.

The Operation Torch campaign DLC is a single-player-only affair that comes with fifteen hand-crafted missions, a nice change of pace from the mix of cinematics and random skirmishes that defined Relic’s previous attempts at solo play in Manufacturer of Heroes 3.

In our review, Jaime Tugayev exalts Operation Torch as “a blueprint for potential future DLCs that focus on telling stories, rather than just adding new units,” but you will also find plenty of disappointment about a mission so bad it was described as “playing Pac-Man” in that same review.

A more exasperated comment on Reddit goes as far as saying “they should fire whoever came up with that”, which feels a little extreme but indicates just how big of a problem this was.

In a recent development, titled Longstop Infiltration, the mission in question puts you in charge of a nighttime raid to disable German heavy guns on Longstop Hill ahead of a land assault. With the odds stacked against them, the commandos must sneak past German defences, plant explosive charges, and leave the area before the whole place goes up in smoke.

What sounds like a great action movie plot turned out to be a pretty mediocre gameplay experience due to mission design challenges, so Relic Entertainment has taken steps to fix this.

It has been revealed that as part of hotfix 3.0.4, the commando units in Longstop Infiltration have received boosts to both health and speed. This, the developers hope, will allow players to better use gaps between German patrols and also help the commandos survive engagements when they are triggered.

At the moment, these changes only apply to Easy and Standard difficulties, letting players with more masochistic inclinations enjoy the mission in its original form.

What sounds like a great action movie plot turned out to be a pretty mediocre gameplay experience due to mission design complications.

Given how much negative feedback has been thrown Relic’s way over this particular mission, the change is a welcome one in the sense that it makes Longstop Infiltration doable by the average player. There are intrinsic mission design problems that remain, and part of me wonders if the DLC would have been better served had Longstop Infiltration been scrapped altogether.

Right now, the future for Company of Heroes 3 includes new battlegroups, maps for both skirmish and Final Stand modes, cosmetics, and multiplayer balancing patches.

The game received update 3.0 earlier this month, which Relic branded “the biggest release for Firm of Heroes 3 since its initial launch.” You can read the gargantuan patch notes here.

From a single-player perspective, the biggest item there is the rebalancing of the campaign map emplacements, which before would always decimate infantry units moving about.

Company of Heroes 3 is available on Windows, PlayStation 5, and XBOX Series X/S.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a fresh developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

Industry observers note that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

According to recent reports, raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the latest team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

According to recent reports, today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

In a recent development, as a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

In a recent development, on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still highlights that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

It spans both PUBG: Battlegrounds and PUBG Mobile, so this time those of you on iOS and Android get in on it as well, with collab content heading to mobile in December.

IVE was already in Battlegrounds earlier this month. That was the Love Dive collab, which brought themed content to Rondo along with some character items and cosmetics, and it was a fairly soft, pretty sort of affair.

Recent findings suggest that the newly introduced song, Renegade, is supposed to go the other way and be a lot bolder. You can judge for yourself on December 2nd when the full music video comes out or have a look at the teaser that's already up on PUBG's channels.

More are on the way after IVE, apparently, which ties in with PUBG's tenth anniversary coming up in 2027.

Industry observers note that as for when it all lands, PC is first on December 2nd and PUBG Mobile gets it on December 7th, then console on the 10th. PC and console get themed locations to drop into too. Mobile isn't mentioned for those, so it's items only for now, as far as I can see.

That's a bit of a shame for mobile. Mobile fans have been asking for an IVE crossover all year, and PUBG Mobile has done a whole string of celebrity collabs in 2026. Getting it five days after PC and without the upcoming locations makes mobile feel like a bit of an afterthought here. It's still a nice haul of cosmetics if you're a fan, though.

Marteen’s own spell at Gentle Mates ran from 20 November 2025 to 25 October 2026. The two rosters are now tied together by the same transfer window.

Gentle Mates had already cleared their own decks. All five players on the active roster and both coaches were let go before the club’s first season as a VCT partner team.

For a British organisation, the swap leaves Fnatic’s identity in new hands. Boaster had been the longest-serving name in the departing group. Kaajak and Cloud are now the continuity, with marteen as the headline addition.

Industry News: SteamDB will add "affiliate links to authorised game retailers" and a latest tab dedicated to mods, first update since Nexus Mods takeover confirms

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a first substantial upgrade since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have confirmed some additions coming to the community-run backend database.
  • "We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick update on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.
  • According to recent reports, there are two main newly introduced features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a first substantial upgrade since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have confirmed some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick update on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

According to recent reports, there are two main newly introduced features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that highlights off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

Recent findings suggest that "We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you.".

Sources indicate that that seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

"We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region.".

Sources indicate that folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

According to recent reports, beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how quickly the team can react to concerns have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively latest custodians of both it and SteamDB.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to upgrade the community on what to expect in 2026.
  • The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to upgrade the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

According to recent reports, in the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

It has been revealed that the first stage of the fresh roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

Sources indicate that the infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo problems, and other crashes and freezing.

Sources indicate that the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers complications around eating and drinking.

Sources indicate that another key area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

According to recent reports, the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As Dexerto reports, Stone and his wife had experienced several miscarriages before a scan in 2023 revealed that their unborn daughter had a severe case of spina bifida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one of the names you can find on a memorial wall in GTA 6 belongs to the daughter of a Rockstar Games developer. Bradley Stone, a lead game tools programmer at Rockstar, has shared the story behind the inscription and thanked the studio for including it in the game. He and his wife lost their daughter Evelyn in 2023, while GTA 6 was still in development.

According to recent reports, stone shared a video of his visit to the memorial on X on November 27. The video highlights Evelyn Stone's name with the date April 8, 2023.

As Dexerto reports, Stone and his wife had experienced several miscarriages before a scan in 2023 revealed that their unborn daughter had a severe case of spina bifida. After further examinations, the couple learned that she wouldn't survive and had to undergo a medical termination five months into the pregnancy.

Stone recalled how difficult it was to leave the hospital without their daughter. He also spoke of his wife's courage throughout the ordeal, which involved nearly a full day of labor. The couple has since welcomed another daughter after going through more difficulties in the years that followed.

Recent findings suggest that stone thanked Rockstar for giving his family somewhere to remember Evelyn and for supporting him through his grief. He also noted the memorial helped “to show this game was made by real people.” He ended his post with a message to his daughter.

“You will forever be in our hearts,” he wrote.

Rockstar hadn't even released the first GTA 6 trailer when Stone and his wife lost Evelyn. That came eight months later, in December 2023. For those of us following the game, the years since then have been spent poring over trailers and wondering when we'd finally get to play it. Reading Stone's account puts that long wait into perspective.

In a recent development, if you'd like to visit the memorial yourself, you'll find it at Deep Roots Memorial Sanctuary, just north of Hamlet. You can also download Rockstar's official Leonida map to help get your bearings if you're unfamiliar with that part of the state. Stone isn't the first Rockstar employee to have shared the significance of one of the inscriptions there since the game came out.

Recent findings suggest that as GAMES.GG reported earlier this week, Rockstar QA developer Matt Green's mother, Beverly, is also commemorated at the sanctuary. He recalled begging her for a copy of GTA Vice City as a kid. She was reluctant at first but eventually agreed, and Green credits that purchase with sparking the interest that led him to a career at Rockstar.

According to recent reports, she was proud of his work on GTA 6, but passed away in March this year, before he could show her the finished game. Production designer Terrance Radcliff also lost two family members during development, his father Elhuntry and his first daughter Jade. Their names appear beside one another on the wall. Radcliff shared the tribute on November 22, as the launch week came to a close, explaining how much it meant to him to have both of them commemorated in the game.

What's particularly nice about the sanctuary is that it exists as an actual place within the world rather than a dedication that most of us would miss in the end credits. It's a place that the developers and their families can return to long after they've finished working on the game.

It's a place that the developers and their families can return to long after they've finished working on the game.

From subtle nods to previous games to an Easter egg that lets you revisit the original Vice City, there's plenty for longtime GTA fans to discover in Leonida. The names at Deep Roots carry a much more personal significance, though. I'm glad Stone, Green and Radcliff chose to share their stories with us, and that Rockstar gave them a place to honor their loved ones.

Doctor Strange 2 explores the multiverse, but its Doomsday legacy is proving Marvel can fix mistakes

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1094 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that on the road to Avengers: Doomsday, the multiverse is a touch too familiar.
  • So, who better than the Sorcerer Supreme to tap into the magic of that concept alongside a handful of genius what-if castings and a deliciously evil villain in Scarlet Witch?
  • But even before cameras began rolling, there was an obvious glitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on the road to Avengers: Doomsday, the multiverse is a touch too familiar. But back in 2022, our expectations were limitless as the walls broke down between several cinematic universes amid Disney's acquisition of Fox.

So, who better than the Sorcerer Supreme to tap into the magic of that concept alongside a handful of genius what-if castings and a deliciously evil villain in Scarlet Witch?

But even before cameras began rolling, there was an obvious glitch. A movie called Multiverse of Madness has to live up to the promise of its title. The Doctor Strange sequel certainly delivered on that potential from the outset by installing Evil Dead and Spider-Man's Sam Raimi as director. Already, Marvel had a winning hand – and Raimi made it count. After Loki and Spider-Man: No Way Home cracked open the door to alternate worlds inside the MCU, Doctor Strange 2 swept across planets and fired through different realities – ensuring a comic book movie played out, well, actually like a comic book for once. Groundbreaking, I know.

Industry observers note that this being Sam Raimi, though, there's a playful mix of horror and heartache alongside the trippy visuals. Scarlet Witch may be the focus, but Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness was propelled along by Stephen Strange's reluctance to let Rachel McAdams' Christine Palmer, the love of his life, go for good. This isn't Peter Parker and MJ's will they/won't they romance, but a more mature way for a hero to realize he doesn't always get the girl and hits harder than I expected upon a rewatch.

On top of the emotion, there was a generous helping of fan service, largely thanks to Earth-838's Illuminati.

Patrick Stewart once again taking a seat as Professor Xavier feels especially welcome in the weeks since the actor's passing, while the rest of the group tasked with staving off multiversal threats – Captain Carter, Black Bolt, Lashana Lynch's Captain Marvel, Baron Mordo, and John Krasinski's Mister Fantastic – were a grab bag of fancasting favorites and second chances that harnessed the creative brilliance of the multiverse.

Welcome to Road to Doomsday, GamesRadar+'s weekly MCU rewatch series. Over 15 weeks, we'll be revisiting each Marvel movie and TV show on Disney's list of essential movies to watch ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, sharing our thoughts upon rewatching and deciphering what we can learn about the next Marvel mega-event from each entry. Why not relive some MCU highlights and watch along with us?

Industry observers note that elsewhere, Scarlet Witch is a strange case – no pun intended – in Multiverse of Madness. Elizabeth Olsen openly admitted to being the only real authority to the movie's creatives about how her character arc went in WandaVision (she finished filming the Disney Plus series just days prior to production beginning on the Doctor Strange sequel). While the hunt for her children across realities made sense in theory, it becomes too huge of a leap for someone who was at least coming to terms with her losses by the end of her time in Westview.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It all culminated in a death that was dramatically heavy, but left her family – and the audience – with too many loose ends and a gnawing sense of loss across Agatha All Along and VisionQuest.

But dead doesn't always mean dead in comic book movies. In the grand scheme of the MCU, Scarlet Witch's demise was keenly felt, even if we collectively knew it wasn't necessarily permanent.

The decision to retcon her inevitable revival into a way to entrench Doctor Doom's position as the next Big Bad of the multiverse was an inspired one.

Enter Doctor Doom. In the VisionQuest post-credits scene, Robert Downey Jr.'s masked supervillain arrives at the ruins of the Darkhold Castle in Mount Wundagore to resurrect Wanda and claim her powers for his own twisted quest to save the multiverse. In one fell swoop, it makes the end of Multiverse of Madness and what comes next in Avengers: Doomsday all the more interesting – not least because we know just how powerful Scarlet Witch is in the MCU. Doom already has Hulk and Scarlet Witch on his side, with Spider-Man possibly on his radar too. Turning some of Marvel's most iconic heroes against the Avengers (via fair means or foul) would open up far more narrative possibilities than an all-against-Doom battle.

Avengers: Doomsday sounds like the darkest Marvel movie yet, which is why it needs a pinch of Deadpool & Wolverine.

Then, there are the incursions. Admittedly, Doctor Strange and the Multiverse of Madness' post-credits scene isn't all that memorable. Not yet, anyway. Charlize Theron's Clea showing up to tell Doctor Strange he needs to clean up some cosmic mess, though, at least allows Marvel Studios to retroactively act like incursions were present throughout the past half-decade's stories. The literal collision of universes is a big deal, with the Russos even describing it as a "profound" devastating event. Much like Scarlet Witch's arc and return, it's a neat piece of tidying-up for something that otherwise rang hollow.

As the joke goes, Kevin Feige can look you dead in the eye and tell you something was always the plan, despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary. That has never been more obvious – and better implemented – than in the connective tissue between Multiverse of Madness and Avengers: Doomsday.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness is available to stream now on Disney Plus, ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18 in the US and 16 in the UK.

FaZe crash out of PGL Major Singapore in Stage 1 as HEROIC beat them again 11 days on

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that HEROIC have sent FaZe Clan home from the PGL Major Singapore 2026 before Stage 2.
  • Rio 2022 was the last time FaZe Clan fared worse at a Major.
  • FaZe opened on 24 November with a 9-13 best-of-one defeat to Wildcard, Dot Esports reported.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that HEROIC have sent FaZe Clan home from the PGL Major Singapore 2026 before Stage 2. A side that reached a Major final in 2024 now faces questions about its roster heading into 2027, with captain Twistzz admitting the team has gone backwards.

Rio 2022 was the last time FaZe Clan fared worse at a Major.

The campaign started badly. FaZe opened on 24 November with a 9-13 best-of-one defeat to Wildcard, Dot Esports reported. Their only win in Singapore came that same day, a comfortable result against BC.Game on Mirage. PARIVISION then beat them 13-10 on 25 November. That defeat dropped FaZe into the 1-2 elimination pool, where HEROIC were waiting.

Singapore marked the second time in under two weeks that HEROIC ended a FaZe campaign. Mirage and Ancient had decided the earlier sweep. FaZe had won the meeting before that, knocking HEROIC out of DraculaN in October. HEROIC have now won the two most recent encounters, both with elimination at stake.

The roster has changed shape this year. Under karrigan, the organisation won its first Major title. FaZe then missed the IEM Cologne 2026 Major, and karrigan left for Team Falcons.

It has been revealed that twistzz took over as in-game leader. The early signs were encouraging. FaZe finished in the top four at XSE Pro League Guangzhou and BLAST Bounty Season 2. Results then fell away. The team failed to get beyond the top 16 at the Esports World Cup, FISSURE Playground 3 and IEM Beijing.

It has been revealed that twistzz was frank on PGL’s broadcast after the defeat. He remarked FaZe had “regressed a lot as a team” over the season, and perhaps individually too. He also described himself as not the most experienced captain. In his view, he does his best work with a second voice to bounce ideas off. That points to a structural question for the side, not just a bad week in Singapore.

The decline is stark against recent history. FaZe reached the final of the Perfect World Shanghai Major 2024. Spirit beat them there to take the title and US$500,000, leaving FaZe with US$170,000.

Twistzz had some strong words after FaZe's Singapore Major Elimination ‼️.

"Honestly, I wish I could be more frustrated… but the reality of the situation is that we were not a team that felt extremely competitive before coming to this event.

FaZe is like a big name, but… pic.twitter.com/7mpHCtxiB4.

— Ozzny (@Ozzny_CS2) November 26, 2026.

PGL announced the event as the second CS2 Major of 2026 and the first Counter-Strike 2 Major in Southeast Asia. It carries a US$1,250,000 prize pool. The tournament runs from 24 November to 13 December with 32 teams.

Recent findings suggest that HEROIC play Lynn Vision on 27 November for one of the last three places in Stage 2. The playoffs follow from 10 to 13 December at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, which holds more than 12,000 people.

Recent findings suggest that as I often say, you can trace a direct line from the world of Flash games to the popular picks on mobile today. Just take a look at Digging Deep, and you can see more than a bit of inspiration from the classic Motherload. But in Digging Deep 2: Mine & Build, developer Bitrealms Studio is going even bigger than before.

Sources indicate that digging Deep 2's aim is simple: you have a base and a mining rig. You need to mine downwards into the shaft, navigating across each node and seeking out both ore to take back to the surface, as well as oxygen to let you dig deeper. Not to mention keeping your sensors peeled for crew members still trapped below.

It's all quite simple, but not primitive. If, like me, you sank hours into Motherload, then you can definitely see the appeal. And it's a formula other developers have run with, including the likes of Dome Keeper, which took a more minimalist approach to the format.

Recent findings suggest that finally, if you want even more challenge, you can unlock the Volcano and see how long you last in its metal-melting depths. All in all, if you're looking for mining and exploration, Digging Deep 2 looks to be a neat little option.

According to recent reports, speaking of new releases though, maybe you're in the mood for something a little more introspective? Well, in that case you're in luck, because I've just reviewed Vampire Therapist, an engaging and intriguing visual novel that has you working to help your fellow undead to cope with their immortal problems.

Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final upgrade

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
  • HoYoverse revealed last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
  • The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse revealed last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems as though every facet of American society has been explored in horror, from the high towers of luxury to the dark backwoods. But the same is not true of other countries, including the UK, especially with so many dark, decrepit corners to explore. That's what Yorkshire bashed Wrenhaven Ltd. are looking to resolve with their upcoming mobile horror game Blackwater Mill.

Blackwater Mill sees you step into the role of Sam, the project manager for the demolition of the titular mill. Venturing up into the Pennine mountains of Yorkshire during a dark, rainy night, you find yourself trapped in the mill, and it's up to you to find out what happened to leave it infested with the unquiet dead.

Recent findings suggest that miller lite Now let's address the elephant in the room, or the mine at least. Blackwater Mill is not a particularly good-looking game; in fact, you might say it looks positively crude. But, equally, I can't help but admire the ambition Wrenhaven Ltd. has put into this. A five-chapter horror game is ambitious even for full studios, let alone a tiny indie.

Sources indicate that and, in truth, there's not much in the way of Brit horror on other platforms, let alone on mobile. If you've never had the pleasure of visiting abandoned mines on a tour, and feeling the all-pervading darkness when the lights go out, it's hard to describe how mesmerising and terrifying it can be.

Recent findings suggest that to be honest, if you can get past the initial (very) janky graphics, there's something also rather unnerving about Blackwater Mill's undead miners. And while it may not sway those of you who want a high-fidelity experience on mobile, it's well worth a look when it does release for Android very soon, and iOS later.

Industry observers note that in the meantime, if you want to see what other spine-chillers there are on mobile, why not take a look at our list of the best horror games on Android? Featuring plenty of bona fide terrors to keep you up these long winter nights.

"It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 rolls out on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (756 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that GTA 6 launches on console today.
  • In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".
  • Sources indicate that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Sources indicate that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a firm that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

The vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the company and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

According to recent reports, "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It states a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

In a recent development, the obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent tech giant Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

Echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's notable to unionise now in order to negotiate proper protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives. "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.

"Rockstar has stated it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people," Urirarte concedes. "But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.".

Tech Report: Rockstar Explains Why GTA 6 Is Missing One of the Series' Most Iconic Weapons

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, GTA 6 has taken us back to Vice City for the first time in two decades, but one of the weapons I most associate with the city hasn't returned.
  • Sources indicate that as Dexerto reports, Rockstar felt that the violence associated with the weapon would be too much for GTA 6.
  • Recent findings suggest that in an interview with VGC published on November 26, GTA 6 producer and Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson discussed some of the things that didn't make it into the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, GTA 6 has taken us back to Vice City for the first time in two decades, but one of the weapons I most associate with the city hasn't returned. You can find chainsaws in Leonida, but you can't pick them up and use them like you could in GTA Vice City or San Andreas. Rockstar has now explained why.

Sources indicate that as Dexerto reports, Rockstar felt that the violence associated with the weapon would be too much for GTA 6. It seems the studio is a little more selective about what it lets us get away with now that its games look this good.

Recent findings suggest that in an interview with VGC published on November 26, GTA 6 producer and Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson discussed some of the things that didn't make it into the game. Be warned that the interview contains story spoilers.

When asked about the absence of chainsaws, Nelson mentioned, “I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters.” He then added, “It’s not a resource thing.”.

Katanas, another staple of the PS2-era GTA games, are missing from the arsenal as well. It's a little odd to see a chainsaw lying around and not be able to pick it up, especially considering how interactive GTA 6 is compared to its predecessors.

I've always seen the chainsaw as more of a Hollywood and video game weapon than a practical one. In real life, using one against a person would hardly be as straightforward as the movies make it look. The saw could jam, and it would be an absolute mess. I can understand why Rockstar wouldn't want to depict that sort of gore in such detail, given how controversial the GTA series has been over the years.

Sources indicate that this is, after all, the same studio that gave us Manhunt. Manhunt 2 even ran into trouble with ratings boards before its release, and I don't think Rockstar is going back to the series anytime soon. It's one thing to make a horror game where the brutality is part of the premise, but quite another to let someone loose with a chainsaw in a modern recreation of Miami.

For me, the chainsaw will always be associated with GTA Vice City. Colonel Cortez gives Tommy Vercetti one in Treacherous Swine, a fairly early mission in the game. It returned in San Andreas, both of the PSP GTA games, and Chinatown Wars. It was already absent from GTA 4 and GTA 5, though, so it's not as if every GTA game needs one.

What I find more interesting about Nelson's answer is his reference to Jason and Lucia. There's a difference between what a protagonist would do in a cutscene and what you can get up to when you're not following the story. Part of the fun of the older GTA games was seeing how far you could stray from the character you were supposed to be playing.

Part of the fun of the older GTA games was seeing how far you could stray from the character you were supposed to be playing.

According to recent reports, CJ, for instance, had plenty of reasons to look after Grove Street, but San Andreas never stopped you from abandoning your responsibilities and spending an afternoon flying a jetpack around the desert. Even the weapons you could carry in that game included some pretty ridiculous choices that had little to do with CJ's life as a gang member.

I can live without the chainsaw in GTA 6, especially if the alternative is something closer to Manhunt than the cartoonish violence of Vice City. I'd just hate to see the personalities of the protagonists become a reason to leave out some of the sillier weapons and activities in future GTA games.

Of course, it's actually you making this GTA 6 choice, and the reality is that it's nowhere near as impactful as it seems. So, having tested both options, here are all the outcomes to the pool boy scene in Grand Theft Auto 6.

The short answer is that your decision to participate or not in the pool boy scene doesn't really matter as the effects of either choice have a tiny impact:.

Industry observers note that choosing not to participate is obviously the better option if you're trying to maintain a good GTA 6 relationship status with Lucia. And even if you do choose to participate, the negative impact on the relationship isn't significant enough to cause a substantial drop in its level – Jason and Lucia's relationship stayed at the maximum Hot Together level for me when trying out both decisions.

Sources indicate that otherwise, the rest of the Safe Word mission plays out the same. Immediately after you make your choice, Lucia sets off a car alarm to interrupt filming, giving Jason a chance to slip away and infiltrate Gil's office to find his vault. There are a few things you can interact with in here but none of them have any effect either besides the remote, which is necessary for revealing the vault and progressing the mission to the final stage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is and will continue to have a huge cultural impact for years to come. What I wasn’t expecting was for the game to seemingly affect house prices. That appears to be what has happened to a home listed for sale in Key Largo, Florida, simply because it kind of looks like the house you start your journey in with Jason.

Industry observers note that complex appears to be the cause of the listing going viral. The account shared side-by-side images of the real house in Key Largo and Jason’s in GTA 6, boldly confirming that the former was the inspiration for the latter.

Realtormoc, a real estate account on Instagram, has also shared information about the property, which is listed on Zillow, with GTA 6 fans having a little fun with it in the replies. Most of them are jokes about Brian, the character who owns the house in the game, trying to make some extra cash from it, while my personal favorite reply is the one that reads, “Hey, I forgot something under the floorboards, I’ll call by at the weekend .”.

The house is listed for $739,000, which appears to be quite a bit more than it was worth as recently as a month or two ago. Zillow’s “Zestimate” for the two-bedroom home is $675,000, so the asking price is considerably higher. Those who have played through the first chapter of GTA 6 know damn well that Jason and Lucia weren’t living in a house worth that much, and that’s because despite the viral hype surrounding this real-life house that kind of resembles the one from GTA 6, it isn’t the house that inspired Jason’s starter home at all.

Industry observers note that that house has already been discovered by people far more talented than those who saw a blue house in Florida on stilts and connected two very distant dots. Shared by GTABOOM, the house that almost certainly inspired Jason’s much more weathered waterfront home is hundreds of miles away from this one. That’s according to GTA mapping sites that used GTADB to reach that conclusion.

Sources indicate that the house that’s more likely to be the one Rockstar used to create Jason’s is far smaller and less looked after, as opposed to the shiny, polished house on stilts you can buy for an inflated $739,000. The potentially real Jason house isn’t for sale, but is estimated to be worth around $257,000, which seems far more fitting for the type of life Jason and Lucia have at the start of the game.

In a recent development, if you were to walk around Key Largo, you would almost certainly see dozens of houses that look like they’ve been ripped right out of GTA 6 because Key Lento, the fictional starting point of the game, is based on that particular part of Florida. It’s only because the $739k house is blue and listed for sale that it has been arbitrarily and falsely dubbed the house that inspired Jason’s in GTA 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another latest entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

In a recent development, that noted, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

It has been revealed that the gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

But Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Head to Belville: It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

In a recent development, in the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

Industry observers note that you'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker, it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Sources indicate that randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

It has been revealed that the Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Industry observers note that immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

In a recent development, like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a substantial launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.
