Breaking: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1218 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that at this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed.
  • In a recent development, A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite.
  • You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that at this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

In a recent development, A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

Almost nothing here works, figuratively and literally. Within three minutes of the opening mission, before Madsen's undercover cop Tanner goes undercover, you're ordered to join some marked police cars to head for a bust – but because the rozzers' primary function is to give chase to you, later on, driving too close crosses their wires, provoking them into blue-on-blue ramming maneuvres. Later, in a motorbike sprint down an inexplicably exploding beach, cartel goons are positioned across the sand, presumably to take drama-enhancing pot shots. They're so slow, however, both to notice your presence and to physically raise their guns, that they're barely out of their idle animations by the time you whizz past. And your own guy isn't much better: an assassination mission, which ends with your target cornered from an elevated position, requires that you take a few steps backwards first, as Tanner can't drop his shootin' arms low enough to land a hit from the balcony he's on.

In a recent development, unlike Vice City's Tommy Vercetti, he can at least swim, which by 2004 standards gives the seaside Miami and Nice maps a fair verisimilitude, particularly when a shot-up boat engine forces the abandoning of ship. No amount of product-of-its-time concessions, though, can account for how woodenly unpalatable the on-foot action is. Controls are stiff and shooting feels meaningless, with zero tangible sense of bullets being sent nor received; killing a man carries all the weight of just shouting at him to lie down, and if it weren't for sound effects and the dwindling health bar, I could park Tanner in front of a firing squad of identically-modelled thugs with almost zero impression that his lungs were filling with Uzi rounds.

Driver, of course, began as a pure wheelman sim, later installments only letting you hoof it after someone at developers Reflections began smelling that Rockstar money. It was therefore always unlikely, even for the purported GTA killer, that this would achieve action-adventure sophistication in its bipedal bits. Even so, god, it's woeful. Stingy checkpointing also means that failure is often punished by having to replay those tedious, flavourless shootouts in full.

The driving is better, which is a bit like saying there's decent cheese in this cheese and smallpox toastie. It's reasonably slidey, when throwing the back end through a curving French alleyway, and in contrast to the gunplay, there is a somewhat realised tactility to ploughing around in two tonnes of rolling metal. It has problems of its own, mind. Cars feel okay when they're moving, but contact and crashes are leaden, sluggish, visually underwhelming occasions that I would call non-events, were they not so slow to recover from that a single nasty impact can scupper a timed mission. Granted, I rapidly re-learned how vital it is to keep both eyes on the road, as other vehicles, pedestrians, lamposts, and other detritus tend to pop into existence some mere fifty feet in front of my speeding bumper.

In a recent development, the result, of both this graphical shortcoming and the overly punishing crashes, is a getaway car sim that too often encourages you to drive like cataract-ridden grandparent. Worse, whoever put Letty Ortiz in a lunchbox must have also been in charge of the engine noises, producing an array of miserable high-rev dins – especially for the motorbikes, which screech like amateurishly autotuned vacuum cleaners. There are also shades of that deranged cop AI in ordinary commuters, who I've repeatedly seen swerving and slaloming around empty lanes, seemingly for no reason beyond violent confusion.

Strangely enough, my 2026 return has largely dodged the game's infamous glitchiness, the worst instance of physics defiance being a garage door that appeared to lift Tanner into the air before propelling him, incorporeally, through the car shed's roof. I recall much worse, from the days when I'd have my dad rent it for me from Blockbuster. Mission-critical NPCs getting stuck on walls; flipped pursuit cars spinning endlessly; getting flung into space when walking on an overturned vehicle (a common occurrence, given the actual 'crawling out' animation sometimes failed to play, the game instead teleporting you onto the spring-loaded underside instead).

Industry observers note that I've thus far escaped these, but as far as I know, they're still lurking dormant, and none of what I've witnessed with adult eyes has been funny or stupid enough to imbue Driv3r 3 The Third with a Wiseauean so-bad-it's-good quality. It's just bad. It was always bad. Why did I even entertain the possibility that it wasn't bad?

Reflections, to their credit, accepted their folly. Narratively unrelated sequel Driver: Parallel Lines tucked away a bin full of discarded copies, at least until Ubisoft bought up the series and patched it out, and for all the fantastical coma silliness of direct followup Driver: San Francisco, that was sensible enough to keep Tanner where he best belongs: hands on the wheel, foot on the gas, gun holstered. And was a far, far better game for it, too.

It has been revealed that as 2011's San Francisco launch also remains the most recent Driver release, I regretfully can't end with the assurance that DrIIIver's legacy is a mere blip on a redeemed franchise. That stain stank, and did for ages, very possibly to the extent that GTA's one-time biggest rival never recovered.

Still, even if Reflections couldn't fully turn around their fortunes, the consistent improvement from this to Parallel Lines to San Francisco showed that they did learn something. Maybe so too did anyone else who went on to make an open-world action game. Which wouldn't be the worst outcome; after all, those who do not learn from gnarled, stinking wrecks like this are doomed to repeat them.

GTA 6: How to Fast Travel

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (464 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it comes to open world games, there’s nothing quite as dense as Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • The obvious question a lot of people might have is “is there fast travel in Grand Theft Auto 6?” This is a massive game with a lot of things to see and do.
  • Sources indicate that you’ll probably go through a good portion of the game not realizing this, but there is indeed a fast travel system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to open world games, there’s nothing quite as dense as Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar has created one of the most impressive open world games ever, with so much to see and do. It becomes incredibly immersive, to the point where sometimes you want a little more game in the game. One specific feature that is a bit unconventional is the fast travel system, but just how do you do it?

The obvious question a lot of people might have is “is there fast travel in Grand Theft Auto 6?” This is a massive game with a lot of things to see and do. It’s one of the most densely packed games we’ve ever played, and being an open world, one would expect there to be some sort of fast travel system.

Sources indicate that you’ll probably go through a good portion of the game not realizing this, but there is indeed a fast travel system. This is because, even though it’s introduced to you early in the game, it’s something easily overlooked. With that said, it does come with a bit of a caveat to the point, especially early on, it’s not really worth using.

With all of that noted, the way you can fast travel is through your phone. First, you will need to put a destination on your map. It can be a custom pin, or it can be a specific location such as a mission marker or clothing store.

It has been revealed that once you have this selected, bring up your phone and select the RydeMe app. This will bring up a standard menu showing how much it will cost to travel that distance you inputed (you can change the destination in this menu) along with ordering a Premium Ryde.

Select the ride and a car will appear shortly. Getting in, though, won’t immediately teleport you to that location. Instead, there will be dialogue, especially if you’re with your partner, and sometimes it is worth it to listen.

Sources indicate that with that said, if you want to actually teleport, you can pay the driver an extra $100 to skip the ride and get there immediately. The downside is obviously, early on, this is an expensive way of traveling. Also, it will pass time considerably because the car itself will take a long time to get to the destination without breaking any rules.

Whether or not you want to use the teleport system in GTA 6 will probably be determined how far a place is located, as anything under 4 or 5 miles generally isn’t worth paying for, but when it gets above that, it can be a bit of a stretch – unless you want to take a helicopter or plane.

📅 04 Mar 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (425 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vg247 ↗ Open Full Page

The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a latest in-game currency to pay for them

📅 04 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.
  • The two upcoming features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17.
  • The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two upcoming destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two upcoming features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature rolls out, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Recent findings suggest that alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It has been revealed that it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

According to recent reports, in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis mentioned that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods.
  • The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.
  • Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods. They're all special custom builds of stock guns and weapons with unique skins, but some of them are way more worth the trouble to hunt down than others. You'll find some of them easily—every Ammu-Nation has a unique gun sitting out for you to buy. The best unique weapons are a little more hidden. There are treasure hunts and easter eggs and a whole lot that you'll grab by fighting your way through a gang hideout.

The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.

Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38.

This is the easiest unique weapon to grab right at the start of the game and totally worth the boat ride to grab it. There isn't even any combat to get to it, like many of these other uniques. The Assassin Nipper comes with a suppressor attachment, which is a really expensive mod to buy early in the game. Pick it up as soon as you've got free range in Key Lento from an old shipwreck in the Permit Keys near the military base location.

In a recent development, another great Chapter 1 snag is this sniper rifle at a Kingfisher hideout. The combat to get it is minimal (don't get between that tiger and its prey) so it's easy to pick up early. It's a bolt action that can't equip a silencer, so it isn't exactly a stealth tool, but it can help Jason pick off gangsters in a hideout before even going inside. It comes with a stock and a basic dot sight.

A variant of the Vom Feur V5FC, found in Port Gellhorn at a Kolt gang hideout. It's up on the top floor of the motel by the La Cascara Motel safe, so you pretty much have to complete this illegal operation to grab it. I recommend coming up the south stairwell that's less guarded and hugging the outer walkways to get most of the way to the loot room by stealth. It's worth it though. The Scrapper is a silenced longarm SMG fairly early in the game with an extended mag and a flashy paint job.

Sources indicate that this Duke Carbine variant doesn't have a suppressor but it is quite high accuracy for a full auto assault rifle with a heavy stock and 7" pistol barrel mod. The Kolt 556 is easier to smash and grab than the Scrapper, though. You've got to fight in and out of the Kolt stash house, but it's a small joint so it's not too hard to get away clean. It's in a gun case on a kitchen table near the safe full of pills.

She likes long fantasy books, longer RPGs, can't stop playing co-op survival crafting games, and has spent a number of hours she refuses to count building houses in The Sims games for over 20 years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bucky Barnes actor Sebastian Stan has defended Thunderbolts after its weaker box office performance.

The film grossed $382 million, which, while not an outright disaster, also isn't a stellar return for Marvel.

Recent findings suggest that "I think it's just when you've had a studio and you've had Marvel, and it's been so many years where they've just been knocking it out of the park, a $350 million global number just suddenly doesn't seem that much. But it's insane how much money that is, you know?" Stan said on the Next Best Picture podcast.

"So, I don't know, I still felt like for us it felt like a success," he continued. "I know a lot of care went into that and it had more nuance to it in terms of, I guess, than some of the recent ones. I don't know, from my point of view at least. Like, dealing with real issues like mental health and depression and so on. They're just a good group of people.".

Stan will soon return in Avengers: Doomsday, a crossover for the ages that puts the Avengers, Thunderbolts, Fantastic Four, and the X-Men up against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

"We love this film. We've poured a lot into it. We've had seven years to think about it. We've got Robert back, greatest actor in the world," co-director Joe Russo remarked recently. "I think it is unlike any movie that's been made in the Marvel universe up to this point. It's tonally very different. It's very surprising, and I think the audience is going to be very surprised when they see the movie.".

Doomsday arrives this December 18. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows for everything else that's on the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What do you do when all hope seems lost, and you're the only one left? Well, clearly you go all out in your tracked war machine and hope to take the enemy down before they do the same to you! And that fast-paced, heavy metal experience is precisely what top-down tank sim Ironclad: Battle Tank promises to provide.

Ironclad: Battle Tank is as straightforward an experience as you can get, and about as subtle about it as, well, a tank. You play as the last lone machine in the fight against the Iron Fleet. Dropped behind enemy lines, each run pits you against bosses in your fight to reach the Citadel and the enormous Dominator that guards it to try and end the war once and for all.

Ironclad: Battle Tank is a refreshingly simple concept for a mobile game, and one that really feels like a throwback to the days of arcade vehicle sims like the Desert Strike series.

In a recent development, presently in closed alpha, Ironclad: Battle Tank is expected to land on Android sometime in 2027, with no current prepares in place for iOS. But watch this space, because if Ironclad turns out to be a rock-solid (metal-solid?) take on the genre, we'll be sure to inform you when it hits iPhone!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that funky feudal family frolic Crusader Kings 3 got its second major expansion of the year this week. It's called Silk and Silver (read my impressions), is all about merchant republics, and shipped alongside a beefy free update to the base game which - while largely focused on overhauling economics - also has some funny patch notes and features worth being aware of.

The main features of the free 'Florin' enhancement are outlined by Paradox in the video above, and unless you're really into the nitty gritty details of realm and wealth management, there's one bit of it which stands out. The option to play as a landless adventurer has finally made its way into the base game, as Paradox promised earlier this year.

This means you can kick off a playthrough as a lowborn leader of a travelling band or a wandering noble with claims on realms ruled by others. Originally locked behind the Roads to Power DLC, the option to start off this way or end up living if you end up deposed from your throne of choice is a great addition to the story arc of any CK3 run. No longer are you glued to the throne from day one to the day you quit for good - power's a privilege which can be earned and revoked depending on what you get up to. Though, it's worth noting that only three ways of operating as a landless adventurer are being made free to access with this enhancement. You can be an aimless wanderers, sword-toting mercenaries, or scholars. If you want your band to earn their living as explorers, free booters, or legitimists, you'll still need Roads to Power.

GTA 6: How to Get into the Apocalypse Bunker

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What’s Grand Theft Auto 6 without a conspiracy theorist character?
  • The bunker in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a little trickier to find just because it doesn’t quite point you in the right direction.
  • Recent findings suggest that the bunker in question is located in North Leonard County.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What’s Grand Theft Auto 6 without a conspiracy theorist character? That’s exactly who Freddie is, a man with his own podcast, and he’s ready for the apocalypse in his major bunker. Unfortunately, you won’t know where to find Freddie as his location is somewhat obscure. There’s nothing to point you in the right direction, but thankfully, that’s why we’re here. We know exactly where to find this bunker, but be warned: it’s not as easy to breach as most hideouts.

The bunker in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a little trickier to find just because it doesn’t quite point you in the right direction. This isn’t part of a main quest, let alone a side quest, but instead is something that has to be found by exploring.

Recent findings suggest that the bunker in question is located in North Leonard County. This section of the map can be found east of North Kelly County and northwest of Vice City itself. The biggest landmark you can look for on the map is Lake Leonida. The bunker can be found on the northwest road closest to it. You see several dark-colored buildings on the map.

Upon driving up to it, though, you will notice that it is completely fortified with an intercom and an automated message saying automated defenses will end you if you attempt to get in.

Sources indicate that being locked away, there will be the temptation to get in. Thankfully, the first time you do this, it’s relatively easy. If you head to the northeast corner of the bunker’s fence, you will find a water tower with a multi-ladder climb.

Climb up the first ladder and on the small platform, jump over the fence onto the shack below. Congratulations; you have successfully breached the defenses. Unfortunately, it’s not over quite yet. This is because there will be additional defenses set up.

Specifically, there will be landmines spread across the property. The best you can do is go down the road towards the bunker and keep an eye out on the ground. You will hear beeping and a red dot on the mine when you get too close.

In a recent development, when you get close to the bunker, drones will be activated. Simply shoot the two down before they get too close as they will explode and deal a good deal of damage. Afterward, jump down the small slope and walk up to the bunker.

It has been revealed that the resident, Freddie, isn’t happy you have got as far as you have, but sees it as a challenge to up his defenses. He will say he will text you when he has installed a better system. Simply wait until he texts you before heading back.

The second time is a little trickier to get in only because he has blocked ladder access to the water tower. Thankfully, he left some excavating tools out in the northwest of the perimeter.

There will be a truck with a large bed, and a bulldozer. Park the truck close to the electric fence and then use the bulldozer’s blade to lift the bed of the truck until it’s slightly above the fence. Jump on the truck and into the bed and then hop over the fence. It’s best to set this up near the water tower to avoid some mines.

In a recent development, speaking of which, the mines are now a little harder to detect. This is because they’re buried slightly further underground, and you can’t see the red light when you get near them. You will still be able to hear it, but it’s best to use your Focus Mode to see them as they light up.

Recent findings suggest that moving down the road, avoiding the significantly more placed mines, the drones attack has also been adjusted. He will still send two waves of them, but instead of one at a time, the first wave has two drones and the second has three.

According to recent reports, after taking care of them, jump down the slope again and approach the bunker for you to meet Freddie for the first time. Congratulations! You can now enter the bunker and even hang out with the apocalypse-ready Freddie.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the big Diablo 4 Developer Enhancement has indeed delivered the goods.
  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the big Diablo 4 Developer Enhancement has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

According to recent reports, when you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a fresh event that rewards you for killing enemies rapidly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a fresh activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

In a recent development, anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

Recent findings suggest that there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

In a recent development, the other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

According to recent reports, even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

It has been revealed that the trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the fresh class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

It has been revealed that show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.

In a recent development, per the Steam page, it claims to have turned the above advert format into a whole latest "deeply strategic genre", the "gates shooter", by stirring in "elements of roguelikes and bullet heavens". I need somebody to authenticate whether this is a truthful statement, or developer TinyToad pulling a fast one. In the meantime, I'll say that 1) I have now managed to kill several ogres, 2) I like Korridor's electro-metal soundtrack.

In Korridor, you're a bald medieval monk garbed in Poundshop Adeptus Astartes platemail. You've woken up in a dungeon of mysterious provenance, and must walk very slowly down its corridors korridors while shooting and punching goblins, wraiths and demons hurrying the other way. Each enemy has a numerical health indicator, and the basic challenge is working out whether you can empty it before they walk into you – which costs you a proportionate amount of health, mitigated by armour. As you go, you'll walk through a choice of gates that grant buffs such as faster health regen, bullet penetration, or nippier horizontal motion.

The fact that you don't control how fast the monk trudges vertically allows the game to synch the onslaught pretty tightly to the thudding, growling score. It reminds me a little of Thumper, though it isn't nearly so invigoratingly malevolent. So far. At intervals, the beat thickens and all the enemies burst into a sprint, throwing their arms up and conveying the strong impression that they are more running away from something than running at you. There's clearly a dreadful entity at the far end of the dungeon. Perhaps it is another overdressed monk with an even bigger gun.

Is this how those mobile games actually work? If it is, then alas and alack, all is lost. I've finally succumbed to those adverts, and all it took was some disingenuous Steam copy promising to place them at a critical remove. Curse you, TinyToad. Curse you and your gates. If you were actually a toad, I'd step on you. Still, now that we've broken the ice, can you please make another game in which I get to play one of those gloating giantesses in Hero Wars? Because I know some people who dig that kind of thing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 17-year-old girl who had been missing for more than a year was rescued and returned home by the FBI after a friend she made while playing Among Us, and his mother, were able to track down her location and pass it along to law enforcement.
  • Landon Tresp told the BBC that he and the anonymous girl "kind of just clicked" when they started chatting online while playing Among Us.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 17-year-old girl who had been missing for more than a year was rescued and returned home by the FBI after a friend she made while playing Among Us, and his mother, were able to track down her location and pass it along to law enforcement.

Landon Tresp told the BBC that he and the anonymous girl "kind of just clicked" when they started chatting online while playing Among Us. She eventually told Tresp she was a runaway who'd been held against her will for more than a year. After learning more, Tresp, 16, told his mother, Khristina, about the exchange; she was initially suspicious, but after speaking with the girl directly on Discord and reading reports of her disappearance, she took action, asking for a piece of mail or document with a full name on it, which the girl provided.

Industry observers note that with that, Khristina began digging into tax and property records to find relevant addresses, which she then used to find photos on real estate sites. She demonstrated the photos to the missing girl on Discord, who picked out the one where she was being held; with that information in hand, Khristina contacted the girl's mother on social media and spoke to her briefly on the telephone, and also received a call from the FBI asking if she could confirm that the girl was still alive.

Sources indicate that "I noted: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her'," Khristina told the BBC. "And she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'.".

Industry observers note that the kidnapped girl contacted Khristina the following morning, after her alleged captor, 39-year-old Adam Hunter Harmel, had left the house. In a conversation monitored by the FBI, she stated she'd met Harmel on social media, where he'd pretended to be disabled and offered to pay her to help him get from Utah to Oregon. When he picked her up, however, he threw her phone into a river, then drove her to Oregon.

Industry observers note that the girl told Khristina that she was kept in his basement and forced to sleep against the wall in his bed, while he kept a knife under his pillow to prevent escape. He gave her a mobile phone that wasn't able to make calls but could connect to wifi, which is how she was able to play online and eventually reach out for help.

While Harmel was out, law enforcement began monitoring his street and house; when the moment came, police had Khristina tell the victim that it was time to make her escape. She was able to leave the house safely and into the custody of state troopers, while Harmel was subsequently arrested and charged with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

A social media post by the Salt Lake City FBI confirmed the outcome, although the crucial role played by Landon and Khristina Tresp was omitted: It indicates only that "the FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the US and in other countries.".

A separate Department of Justice press release, however, acknowledges that "on Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025.".

According to recent reports, khristina and Landon have remained in daily contact with the girl they helped rescue, and they're trying to arrange an in-person meetup as well. "Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina said. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner …it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away. She's doing great for what she's gone through.".

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Revision, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Recent findings suggest that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Revision to actually see it in action.

According to recent reports, the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

In a recent development, lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The open world Rockstar has created for Grand Theft Auto 6 is massive, but it’s not just about the weird random encounters you will find yourself in.
  • In a recent development, unfortunately, like a number of minor characters in the story, there is a scene very late in chapter 4 where his fate seems to be put into your hands.
  • Spoiler warning for anyone who hasn’t reached past the VCI Takedown mission.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The open world Rockstar has created for Grand Theft Auto 6 is massive, but it’s not just about the weird random encounters you will find yourself in. There is a massive, 40+ hour-long story with a whole cast of characters to explore. One of the best characters introduced has to be Raul, a suave thief who Brian introduces to, and one who plays a key component to everything that happens in both chapter 3 and 4.

In a recent development, unfortunately, like a number of minor characters in the story, there is a scene very late in chapter 4 where his fate seems to be put into your hands. We will go over both scenarios, although you might be a bit disappointed with the outcome.

Spoiler warning for anyone who hasn’t reached past the VCI Takedown mission.

It has been revealed that the first option is pretty simple. Raul quickly tells you what happened, specifically, Valentina sold them out and Mendez personally came and tortured him. After that, he tells Lucia and Jason to put him out of his misery.

According to recent reports, this is where the “choice” comes into play. This option will initiate a firefight outside the boat, as whoever finds Raul tied up will shoot him in the head. Thankfully, Raul comes ready for anything and has a gun locker in the other room.

Still, doing this yourself is arguably the best thing to do for Raul as he likely would have been killed more horrifically afterward. Still, if you don’t want to pull the trigger yourself, there is another option.

Despite Raul pleading and begging for Jason and Lucia to put an end to his suffering, there is the option to restrain yourself like you can in various other situations thus far. You don’t have to pull the trigger, but unfortunately, Raul’s fate is secured no matter what.

If you decide you can’t put Raul out of his misery yourself, your partner, specifically whoever doesn’t find Raul in the bathroom, will automatically shoot him instead. It’s a pretty anti-climatic conclusion, all things considered, especially considering the shot itself alerts a task force which is converging on the boat.

In a recent development, in the end, Raul must die for the story to continue, and either Jason or Lucia will be the one who pulls the trigger. It’s just a matter of if you, as the player, does it.

#155204. Industry News: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1832 w)

Industry News: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I don't play video games regularly anymore.
  • Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019.
  • Sources indicate that my relationship with Azeroth began in 2007, when I was ten years old.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth, the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a upcoming legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a newly introduced Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.

Sources indicate that my relationship with Azeroth began in 2007, when I was ten years old. As soon as I inserted the CD-ROM, I knew that I was going to have to vastly increase my timeshare on the family desktop. For the next six years, school attendance, sleep, and quality family time suffered immensely as I battled to balance my newly introduced parallel existence as a member of the Orcish Horde.

It's unremarkable now, but the fact that characters created at WoW's launch are now 22 years old and can still be played in the latest iteration of the game would have been almost inconceivable to many developers at the turn of the century. In the late 1990s and early 2000s, the video game industry was overwhelmingly organised around discrete releases expected to have relatively short lives. For most games, commercial success was concentrated in a brief period surrounding their launch, after which sales declined and eventually ceased. WoW's extraordinary success, and exceedingly long half-life, demonstrated the commercial possibilities and durability of a different model: an evolving, immersive digital environment that players paid to inhabit, year after year. Rather than simply purchasing a finished product, players entered a world that would continue to grow around them. Latest players, after buying the game (and then its subsequent expansions) and paying for a subscription, could begin their adventures in the same world as those who had been there from the beginning, making their way through its ever-expanding geography and history.

The persistence of Azeroth has been the main driver of its abiding allure for me. I have returned to the game time after time, often just to be enveloped in an audiovisual environment that I know so intimately, and which was so formative in my life. But as the WoW universe was continually developed, the game became increasingly unrecognisable from the version I skipped school to play on Windows XP.

What I wanted from the game had also changed. In a turn that would have been completely anathema to my teenage self, I no longer cared about reaching the endgame or having the most competitive character. I stopped caring about the latest raiding content or PvP rankings. Instead, the elements of the game I had once feverishly tried to skip over, like levelling, professions and story, became, ironically, the only parts of the game that I yearned for.

As time unspooled, WoW naturally needed updates to stay fresh. This meant overhauling many of the unwieldy elements of its original design. Much of this was described as 'streamlining' the player experience, making the game less tedious by reducing downtime and, most critically, reliance on other players.

Industry observers note that the original Azeroth emulated the real world in ways that few contemporary games do. Firstly, it was openly unbalanced, with some classes vastly stronger than others, some of which were borderline unplayable. Secondly, it required extraordinary amounts of patience and downtime to navigate. Most importantly, though, it required collaboration with others to get the most out of it. In order to access the latest content, players would have to self-organise into specifically composed groups as major as 40 players large, and schedule lengthy chunks of time each week to make progress.

In a recent development, over time, much of the original social architecture that forced player collaboration was stripped from the game. Adventurers no longer needed to search for and group up with other players from their own server to complete rewarding content. Automated matchmaking systems increasingly did the work for them.

I remember many late nights when I was prevented from doing something quite modest because there were simply not enough players online, or not enough of the right classes. With my ambitions frustrated, I would often have no choice but to log off and try again in the morning. These frustrations were, I only learnt in retrospect, an important byproduct of inhabiting a world that did not exist solely for my benefit. Other people had their own schedules, priorities and ambitions, and my experience of the game depended on those contingencies.

The changes to WoW followed the trajectory of the wider online gaming industry, where players could increasingly be matched instantly with others at any time of day. These were changes that genuinely respected players' time, but the texture and immersion of the game world paid a hefty price. In making the game more convenient, Blizzard had also made it less necessary, and in some respects less possible, to participate in the social world that had once made Azeroth feel so alive.

It became increasingly clear that there was a subset of players, like me, who weren't interested in seeing an old dog learn newly introduced tricks, and just wanted to spend time with the old girl we'd raised from a pup. Even if she did walk slowly, and was a bit blind.

As the years went on, many players moved on with their lives, even if they continued to carry some indelible residue of Azeroth with them. Others created unofficial instances of the original game, known as private servers, and relived those infant years with a knowledge of the world that they could scarcely have imagined possessing when they first entered it. As these servers became increasingly popular, Blizzard, originally very reluctant, eventually launched Classic in 2019, an official revival of the game in something approaching its original 2004 form. Since then, legacy versions of WoW have become popular enough to exist alongside the modern game as a major branch of the franchise.

Re-releasing these legacy versions has been a considerable commercial success. But it also exposed a problem with the project of preservation. The original game, because it is so timeworn, has effectively been 'solved.' Players know almost everything about it, including its most obscure idiosyncrasies, and have found ingenious ways of exploiting them. The uncertainty that once made Azeroth feel so vast and mysterious has been replaced by an extraordinary collective expertise. When new content was added to the game, even the best guilds would spend weeks making no progress. During those early years, players at Azeroth's frontiers had to innovate to find creative ways of tackling novel and seemingly intractable problems.

There are clear limits to simulating a turning back of the clock. Players like me slowly realised that we didn't simply want to return to an earlier, simpler period in Azeroth. We wanted something impossible. Like the characters in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, we wanted to forget what we already knew so that we might experience our birth in Azeroth for the first time all over again.

According to recent reports, woW: Forever is an attempt to solve this problem. Like Old School RuneScape, Forever's undeniable forerunner and a considerable success in its own right, it is an expanded re-release of the original game that imagines an alternate future for Azeroth: one in which the game continues to evolve without abandoning the original texture and mechanics, and one that preserves the social architecture that made it so enriching in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that as I write this, my Orc Warrior is sitting at a Campfire, a new mechanic that allows players to establish communal campsites and contribute profession-specific items that confer temporary bonuses to themselves and others. To receive a benefit from Campfires, adventurers are forced to sit together, a deliberate attempt from Blizzard to encourage interactions between players. It is too early to tell how effective this socialising mechanism will be in the long run, but nearly everyone in my experience so far has been eager to shoot the breeze together. I have already shared a number of conversations with other players, most of whom are thirty- or forty-somethings on a similar nostalgia quest as me.

Industry observers note that I am playing the game on a laptop using a trackpad, caring very little about efficient or optimal progression. Although I suspect a substantial proportion of the player base shares my approach, not everyone has approached the game so casually. At least five players have already reached maximum level, and many others will have meticulously theory-crafted plans designed to skip straight to the endgame. This is a good thing, and the game should be able to support players with different goals. It's key that the game rewards time and effort, but I hope that the modest amount of time I am able to commit will allow me to feel like I am on my own meaningful adventure, and not a weak player who is trailing behind.

Many in the community have come to believe, perhaps wishfully, that Forever might escape the trap of vertical progression, in which each newly introduced wave of content supersedes and renders older content redundant. Instead, the promise of horizontal progression, where new content expands the range of meaningful activities and rewards available without continually raising the ceiling of character power, has been latched on to by members of the community, even though Blizzard's messaging in this regard has not been totally clear.

Industry observers note that for players like me, the appeal of horizontal progression is that Azeroth might once again become a place to inhabit, rather than a race to finish. I want to be able to wander off, pursue some obscure profession, or spend an evening doing very little of consequence without feeling that the rest of the world has left me behind. I know I don't have the time to commit to the endgame hamster wheel, and whether Forever will produce a gameworld that meaningfully accommodates players with such different ambitions remains to be seen. But for now, at least, it feels good to be home.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There were a good few indies set for launch in September last year that ended up being delayed to escape the blast radius of Hollow Knight: Silksong.
  • Yesterday, the Silksong dev revealed an upcoming 'Cherry Time' special presentation, promising news and announcements from the studio, and an update on the hotly-anticipated Sea of Sorrow DLC.
  • This time, however, the dev is standing firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There were a good few indies set for launch in September last year that ended up being delayed to escape the blast radius of Hollow Knight: Silksong. Aeternum Game Studios' Metroidvania, Aeterna Lucis, was one such title, pushing its release date to 3rd December 2026 to ensure it was way out of the way of whatever Team Cherry was cooking up. Heh, well...

Yesterday, the Silksong dev revealed an upcoming 'Cherry Time' special presentation, promising news and announcements from the studio, and an update on the hotly-anticipated Sea of Sorrow DLC. The showcase is tomorrow (27th November), so there's every chance that, in dodging the initial launch, Aeterna Lucis has wound up right in the way of the DLC (thanks, Steam Hype).

This time, however, the dev is standing firm. "A lot of people have been waiting for the Queen of Light for a long time now, and we don't want to make them wait any longer," the dev wrote in a message on social media, neatly captioned "Here we go again".

It's all very jokey and light-hearted, with Aeternum even proposing a Silksong bundle if the dates do happen to clash. Still, there's room for a little cursing of fate: "With all the love in the world: is it just us, or does the universe have it in for us?".

You'll find the full statement below, followed by the post from Bluesky:.

Recent findings suggest that A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you declared Silksong. We stepped aside, pushed the whole project back a year and, honestly, it was one of the best decisions we've ever made: the genre had an incredible year, and we got to enjoy Silksong as fans and polish Aeterna Lucis into the game we always dreamed it would be.

Sources indicate that now here we are again, just days from launch. Aeterna Lucis, our new metroidvania, comes out on December 3... and you announce Cherry Time. This time we're staying put. Not to go against you, but because a lot of people have been waiting for the Queen of Light for a long time, and we don't want to make them wait any longer.

Whatever happens on Friday, we'll be watching like any other fan. And if Sea of Sorrow ends up launching on the same day, the real winners will be metroidvania fans.

Recent findings suggest that that said, we have to ask, with all the love in the world: is it just us, or does the universe have it in for us? Hahaha. And since you're about to wreck our lives all over again, the least we can do is make a bundle together.

With all our love (and a little bit of fear), The Aeternum Game Studios team.

While we can't imagine Sea of Sorrow will have quite the industry-shaking impact that the base game did, it sure would be unfortunate to see an indie like Aeterna Lucis caught in the line of fire again. Hey, at least the dev is able to have a laugh with it.

In a recent development, will you be checking out Aeterna Lucis next month, or do you think Silksong might be gobbling up all your time? Let us know in the comments.

[source bsky.app, via steamhype.com].

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially released.
  • The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially released. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

It has been revealed that the open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

According to recent reports, marathon has now officially released, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game right now sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

A new scheduling gap in the Pokémon anime might give us a clue to the Winds and Waves release date.

Serebii founder Joe Merrick pointed out on Bluesky that for the entirety of his time running the fan site, "there has been a latest anime episode each week." However, it was announced today that there will be a nine-month gap between Winter Voyage in December and the new Liko and Roy series in 2027.

In a recent development, "Winds and Waves' obvious schedule changes really messed with things huh," Merrick mentioned. A fresh series of the show typically launch alongside a new mainline game, so delaying the series to October could be taken as evidence that Winds and Waves will launch later in the year.

Of course, it's also possible the anime's hiatus has nothing to do with Winds and Waves, and that the late schedule is intentional. But it lines up with the Pokémon TCG debacle.

Last month, McDonald's accidentally revealed an upcoming collab for its Happy Meals, with 15 fresh cards arriving in November 2027 — interestingly, there are no new Pokémon included whatsoever. Not even the Winds and Waves starters.

The theory goes that the latest set will arrive too soon after Winds and Waves to include any new 'mons, which would line up with the anime releasing in October.

Put it all together, and it looks like Winds and Waves will launch in late 2027, narrowing down the release window.

Until we hear from The Pokémon Company, of course, this is all speculation, so it's worth taking with a grain of salt. However, considering that mainline games traditionally launch in November (or, at the earliest, September), it lines up.

If Winds and Waves has been delayed, explaining the wider-than-usual gap in the anime, then maybe it's for the best. Game Freak could certainly use a little more runway with the mainline games.

We're just a couple weeks away from Marathon's Symbiosis patch, a hefty overhaul patch that's aiming to inject some juice into the shooter's live service appeal with the addition of PvE roguelite and Team Deathmatch modes, new weapons, and even a social hub for hanging out with fellow runners and testing guns at the firing range.

Sources indicate that and that's all great. But today, Bungie dropped a new cinematic that presents its strongest argument for why Symbiosis should have our attention: You can play as a terrifying, sports-car scarlet robot samurai with a sword arm and jet legs.

Recent findings suggest that while Bungie previously revealed Bishop, the new runner shell arriving with Symbiosis, in the update's first gameplay trailer earlier this month, the new cinematic provides a strong sense of the power fantasy it's trying to capture. By which I mean Bungie clearly wants you to feel like a nightmarish apex predator. Like a xenomorph if a xenomorph was bright red and had cool space guns.

In a recent development, as the trailer progresses, we watch as a team of runners is steadily cut down by a Bishop shell's unflinching onslaught: First, one of its members is culled after taking one of Bishop's throwable hacking knives to the neck, which seems to disrupt the target's functions. The next is blasted out of midair while trying to zipline away to safety. The third is hounded by autopistol fire into a position where they can be conveniently pounced on from above.

According to recent reports, but the trailer's peak moment happens as the Bishop prepares to loot one of its kills and is winged by a bullet from a nearby Rook, who evidently hoped to clean up after watching the whole fight pan out. This is proven to be a mistake, because the Bishop settles into a crouch, extending a plasma-edged sword blade from between its knuckles and engaging the jet thrusters in its calves.

Sources indicate that you know that thing in samurai movies where a swordsman does a lunging slash, leaving the body of his opponent to realize that it's been cut down behind him? It's like that. But with robots and jet propulsion. Marathon's going to have iaijutsu, is what I'm saying. Something for us all to look forward to.

Marathon's Symbiosis patch lands on December 8.

  • Industry observers note that today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Industry observers note that today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja stated it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

According to recent reports, the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Recent findings suggest that patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

It has been revealed that speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The employment tribunal over Rockstar's firing of 34 workers last year has come to an end for now, pending a final verdict from the judge. Stated judge hasn't offered a concrete estimate of when her judgement will arrive, but has reportedly asserted that she'll provide it "as rapidly as [she] possibly can".

That's according to People Make Games' Chris Bratt, who's reported on the tribunal throughout the proceedings."I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case," he cited judge Lucy Wiseman as having noted following closing arguments from Rockstar and the union representing the fired staff over the past couple of days. "What I will say is that I will use my best [endeavours] to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Bratt reported that could mean anything from weeks to a few months of waiting, leaving the fired staff looking at more time in the limbo they've occupied throughout the tribunal.

Sources indicate that to recap the arguments Wiseman will have heard, Rockstar accused the fired staff of leaking "confidential information on a public forum", while the Independent Workers’ union of Great Britain (IWGB) union have accused Rockstar of being motivated by union busting in letting the workers go. According to a previous report from People Make Games, discussion of a new tech giant Slack policy in a union-run Discord server preceded the firings.

The fired devs haven't called for supporters to boycott GTA 6 - the game they were working on prior to being let go - in solidarity, but instead to consider buying specially-designed union t-shirts, the proceeds of which will go towards the workers' "Fighting Fund".

Devs still at Rockstar and the IWGB have formed the Rockstar Games Workers Union since their fired colleagues' tribunal proceedings began and are in the midst of a vote on union recognition as of writing.

Industry observers note that writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section this week, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte expressed that it's "hard not to worry about what the future holds" for developers at the studio, with the prospect of layoffs potentially happening now the significant game is out the door concerning staff. Uriarte made clear that, as of the writing of his piece, Rockstar staff "have had no indication that layoffs are coming".

Nintendo has issued a statement acknowledging load time issues on Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy on Switch 2.

In a recent development, the company has promised to released a patch addressing the concerns, citing the long load times that primarily occur when travelling to surface areas. It's also identified an concern in which long loads occur if your network connection is unstable.

While Nintendo works to resolve the challenges, it has advised to play in an environment with a stable network connection.

"In Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy, we have identified an glitch where loading times are longer than expected when traveling to surface areas, including the Rescue Camp. We are presently preparing an revision to address this. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause.

"Additionally, we have identified an issue where launching the game or accessing the "Dandori Challenge" (Dandori Test) may take an extended amount of time if the network connection is unstable. We are at the moment investigating the cause of this issue.

"If you encounter these problems, playing in an environment with a stable network connection may help resolve them.".

Recent findings suggest that pikmin 4 on Switch 2 garnered decent reviews upon release, though it's safe to say that it's not the most beloved upgrade Nintendo has provided for its latest console. Players were immediately put off by the load times, a lack of 60fps, and seemingly slight newly introduced content based on existing levels.

Indeed, Nintendo's latest statement has been met with comments from users demanding that 60fps be added to the game, but the company has not acknowledged this, so it seems unlikely to be included at this time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Try not to get whole armies of Space Marines pasted against the surfaces of planets thanks to your shoddy tactics, please. So ask the bosses of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, who're keen not to have their training workloads doubled because you're a crap general and have gotten a tight-knit force of uber-tough grunts killed unnecessarily, hope as they watch you play. This and other things have been emphasised by a fresh stream showing off over an hour of campaigning in the strategy warhammerer.

Industry observers note that the stream highlighted off "an expansion" of the build that devs Creative Assembly let folks like RPS bossman Julian give a go at Gamescom in the summer, via an Ultramarines campaign in a system called Praevoss. Described as a middle-of-the-road option in terms of system size, Praevoss is home to three conquerable planets and a couple of others that aren't suitable for stompy unit hijinks.

Recent findings suggest that each star system's a "contained campaign", so you hop from one to the next, with certain aspects of your army or skills you've built up carrying over. "First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," the devs explained. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start [point], [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do." Creative assembly have also been able to play around a bit more with difficulty as a result of this setup.

Sources indicate that as the stream properly got going, the devs focused on chatting about unit specialisation, fleet movement, fleet actions, fleet transportation and Space Marine fleet buildings. Your fleet takes the form of big ships which can be parked above a continent on a planet and offer support via reinforcements and bombardment. As far as the Space Marines specifically go, they're designed to be a small force that's tough to kill, rather than a massive one that's able to recover more swiftly and aims to overwhelm with sheer numbers as part of its gameplan.

According to recent reports, "Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the devs said, as if sensing some blunder I might make far in the future. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that." At least it looks like I'll not be losing any ships too, since their presence seems limited to providing support to the ground troops, rather than battling each other high above the planets.

As of right now, Total War: Warhammer 40,000 remains without a release date, but can be wishlisted on Steam if you fancy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 will soon get a latest revision to resolve a number of problems, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most crucial is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Industry observers note that going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Industry observers note that speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis remarked this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in upcoming saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

It has been revealed that you may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a upcoming lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an revision that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently unveiled that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.
