Sources indicate that team Cherry promised us an enhancement on Hollow Knight: Silksong's Sea of Sorrow DLC today, and thankfully it was not a tepid one where the studio gave the expansion a loose release window way off in the future. It was a far firmer reveal confirming that the free addition to Silksong will be here far sooner than you might have expected.

The trailer for Sea of Sorrow was part of today's Cherry Time update, giving us a first look at what horrors Hornet will be up against next. That first look at the expansion was coupled with the reveal that it will be available on December 11, 2026, so in just 13 days. The DLC will be free to all Silksong owners, no matter which platform you play on.

I'm sure Hollow Knight fans wouldn't argue with that decision given the benefit of hindsight, but it made the wait for Silksong especially excruciating.

Recent findings suggest that there is no risk that Sea of Sorrow will be held back and used to complete the Hollow Knight trilogy. The expansion's release isn't even getting pushed into 2027. This time in two weeks, we'll all be playing it, and it won't cost you an extra penny to do so. If you own Silksong, you will get the DLC for free on December 11. And if you don't, the base game is still just $19.99 and is about to get a whole lot bigger.

Giving fans roughly two weeks between announcement and release appears to be a cadence that Team Cherry has settled into. There was roughly a two-week gap between the announcement of Silksong's release date and its launch, and that went incredibly well. I can only imagine repeating that pattern for Sea of Sorrow will have a similar effect, and the sequel will get a huge player count spike on December 11, along with a sales spike between now and then as those who missed out at launch play catch up before Sea of Sorrow arrives.

#155191. I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (904 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games.
  • In a recent development, if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop.
  • Industry observers note that many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too quickly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

In a recent development, if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Industry observers note that many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The matter is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

In a recent development, when I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a upcoming paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

According to recent reports, minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

According to recent reports, romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

What are your favorite video game romances? Let us know in the comments!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that according to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season.
  • Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.
  • On December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that according to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season. Blizzard shoved just about every iconic Diablo 2 boss and item it could think of into the modern game, and, by all accounts, it was one of the best seasons it ever had.

Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.

On December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm. However, the craftable items, like the Enigma chest piece that gives you a free teleport skill, will not carry over.

Industry observers note that even without all the craftable unique items, that's quite a lot of stuff to keep around. Blizzard tends to ditch seasonal additions as soon as a new season starts, and you usually have to wait a while to see them slipped back into the game in a slightly altered form. The overwhelming excitement around the Diablo 2 content must've convinced Blizzard it was worth putting in the work to keep them around.

It has been revealed that I would've been happy if the portal to Tristram, the rickety old town at the center of Diablo 2, was all that came back. Blizzard pulled off an incredibly faithful remake of it, complete with the old guitar theme and the voice of the blacksmith Griswold. And if you follow the hidden steps to make the Hellfire Torch, you'll be able to visit Uber Tristram, a special version of the town where you can square off against all three of the series' major villains, the Prime Evils, at once.

Diablo 4 was always kind of light on hidden quests and bosses, so it's nice to see that Blizzard found a way to bring an key part of the series back. I'll be curious to see what else comes to the game over the next three years before Diablo 5 arrives. The Amazon class will drop next year, but no expansions are planned to fill the gap. Hopefully Blizzard will take this opportunity to experiment with more things like the Diablo 2 anniversary secrets before it moves onto the sequel.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

Recent findings suggest that it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Recent findings suggest that crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

Latest Update: Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • It has been revealed that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

It has been revealed that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

It has been revealed that once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the newly introduced Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Sources indicate that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Industry observers note that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a significant latest upgrade - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.
